cards.text: After the boils (Exodus 9:8-12), the LORD tells Moses, Israel's leader, to get up early, stand before Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and give him the LORD's message: "Let My people go, so that they may worship Me." An early morning meeting, friend? You KNOW it's serious.

cards.question: If Pharaoh says no, the LORD will send all His plagues against Pharaoh, his officials and his people. What does the LORD want Pharaoh to know?

answers.text: There is no one like the LORD in all the earth
Israel is stronger than the army of Egypt
Moses is the greatest prophet in the land

cards.text: Then the LORD tells Pharaoh that by this time He could have stretched out His hand and struck him and his people with a plague to wipe them off the earth. He could have. He hasn't.

cards.question: So why hasn't He? The LORD says He raised Pharaoh up for this very purpose: to display His ___ to him, so that His name might be proclaimed in all the earth.
The LORD tells Pharaoh that he has finally started letting Israel go.

cards.text: Then the LORD gives the warning: "Behold, at this time tomorrow I will rain down the worst hail that has ever fallen on Egypt, from the day it was founded until now." A whole DAY'S notice, friend? In that junk drawer I was stuck in for years, all the notice we ever got was a rattle right before the drawer flew open.

cards.question: Then the LORD tells Pharaoh what to do before the hail comes. What orders should Pharaoh give right now?

answers.text: Shelter the livestock and everything in the field
Drive the livestock away into the wilderness
Gather the people at the palace gates

cards.question: The LORD warns that every man or beast left out in the field will die when the hail comes down.
Some of Pharaoh's officials hurry their servants and livestock to shelter, and others leave them in the field. What makes the difference?

answers.text: Whether they feared the word of the LORD
Whether they lived close to the palace
Whether Moses had warned them himself

cards.text: Then the LORD tells Moses to stretch out his hand toward heaven, so hail falls on all the land of Egypt: on man and beast and every plant of the field. Friend, that's the timer going DING.

cards.question: Moses stretches out his staff toward heaven, and the LORD sends hail. What comes with it?

cards.text: The hail falls with the lightning flashing right through it, and nothing like it had ever been seen in all of Egypt since it became a nation. Friend, I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, and even I'd want to crawl back in for this one.
Throughout the land of Egypt, the hail strikes down everything in the field, both man and beast. That warning comes true, friend, and this part is heavy.

cards.question: The hail beat down the plants in Egypt's fields, but it left the trees alone.
The hail pounds the land of Egypt, but there's one place where it doesn't hail at all: the land where the Israelites live. What is it called?

cards.text: Then Pharaoh summons Moses and Aaron, Moses's brother. "This time I have sinned," he says, and friend, I almost dropped a whole cookie box.

cards.question: Pharaoh tells Moses and Aaron that he has sinned. What does he say about the LORD?
Pharaoh has had enough of God's thunder and hail. What does he ask Moses and Aaron to do?

cards.text: Pharaoh even promises to let them go, and Moses says that once he's left the city, he'll spread out his hands to the LORD and the thunder and hail will stop. Friend, Pharaoh wants this storm GONE, and honestly, I'm right there with him.

cards.question: Moses says the storm will stop so that Pharaoh may know that the earth belongs to the ___.
Moses tells Pharaoh he knows that Pharaoh and his officials finally fear the LORD.

cards.text: The hail destroyed the flax and barley, since the barley was ripe and the flax was in bloom. Of all the weeks to be ready, friend, the barley picked THAT one.

cards.question: Wheat and spelt are late crops, so the hail did not destroy them.

cards.text: Moses leaves Pharaoh, goes out of the city and spreads out his hands to the LORD, and the thunder and hail stop and the rain no longer pours down on the land. Friend, the sky goes from WORST EVER to not a peep.

cards.question: The sky goes quiet, and Pharaoh sees the storm is over. What does he do?

answers.text: He sins again and hardens his heart
He lets the Israelites go at once
He sends Moses a gift of thanks

cards.question: Pharaoh's officials harden their hearts too.

cards.text: So Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he wouldn't let the Israelites go, just as the LORD had said through Moses. Keep your apron on, friend, because this story is a long way from done.
